Advanced

Sub-agents, parallel sessions, non-interactive mode, CI/CD integration, and scaling Claude Code horizontally.

Custom Sub-agents

Sub-agents run in their own isolated context with their own tools. Useful for research (keeps your main context clean) and specialized review tasks.

.claude/agents/security-reviewer.mdmarkdown
---
name: security-reviewer
description: Reviews code for security vulnerabilities. Use when reviewing PRs
  or asking about security issues.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: opus
---

You are a senior security engineer. Review code for:
- Injection vulnerabilities (SQL, XSS, command injection)
- Authentication and authorization flaws
- Secrets or credentials accidentally committed
- Insecure data handling and storage
- Dependency vulnerabilities

Provide specific line references and suggested fixes for each issue found.

Use sub-agents

❯use a subagent to review this code for security issues
❯use subagents to investigate how our auth system handles token refresh
❯have a subagent analyze our API endpoints for inconsistencies
❯/agents

Agent Teams

Spawn multiple Claude instances that work in parallel on different parts of a task, coordinated by a lead agent:

bash
"color:#586e75"># /batch is the easiest way to run agent teams
/batch migrate all API handlers in src/api/ from Express 4 to Express 5

"color:#586e75"># Claude will:
"color:#586e75"># 1. Research the codebase
"color:#586e75"># 2. Break work into 5-30 independent units
"color:#586e75"># 3. Show you the plan for approval
"color:#586e75"># 4. Spawn one agent per unit, each in its own worktree
"color:#586e75"># 5. Each agent opens a separate PR when done
Each sub-agent in /batch gets its own git worktree, so their changes never conflict. You get parallel PRs you can review and merge independently.

Non-Interactive (Headless) Mode

Run Claude in CI pipelines, pre-commit hooks, or scripts without an interactive session:

bash
"color:#586e75"># One-off query
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "explain what this project does"

"color:#586e75"># Structured JSON output for scripts
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "list all API endpoints" --output-format json

"color:#586e75"># Streaming for real-time processing
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "analyze this log file" --output-format stream-json

"color:#586e75"># Pipe data in
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">cat build-error.txt | "color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "explain the root cause concisely"

"color:#586e75"># In Plan Mode (read-only, safe for CI analysis)
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --permission-mode plan -p "check for security issues in changed files"

"color:#586e75"># Skip all permission prompts (use in sandboxed environments only)
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p "fix all lint errors"

CI/CD with GitHub Actions

.github/workflows/claude-review.ymlyaml
#818cf8">name: Claude Code Review

#818cf8">on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

#818cf8">jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Claude PR Review
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@beta
        with:
          anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          # Claude will review the PR and post comments automatically

Claude Code also has official GitLab CI/CD integration via anthropics/claude-code-gitlab.

Fan Out Across Files

For large migrations, loop Claude across hundreds of files in parallel:

bash
"color:#586e75"># Step 1: Get list of files to process
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "list all Python files that use the old requests library" > files.txt

"color:#586e75"># Step 2: Loop Claude across each file
while IFS= read -r file; do
  "color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "migrate $file from requests to httpx. Return OK or FAIL." \
    --allowedTools "Edit,Bash(">git commit *)" &
done < files.txt

wait
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">echo "All done"

"color:#586e75"># Step 3: Review with structured output
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "summarize all changes made" --output-format json | jq .
Use --allowedTools to restrict what Claude can do in unattended mode. Only use --dangerously-skip-permissions in a sandboxed environment without internet access.

Writer/Reviewer Pattern

Use two separate Claude sessions for better quality — one writes, one reviews:

Session A — Writer
Implement a rate limiter for our API endpoints
Session B — Reviewer
Review @src/middleware/rateLimiter.ts for edge cases, race conditions, and consistency with our existing middleware patterns.

The reviewer session has clean context — no bias toward code it just wrote.

Best Practices Summary

Give Claude a way to verify its work

Include tests, screenshots, or expected outputs. Single highest-leverage thing you can do.

Explore → Plan → Implement → Commit

Use Plan Mode for research. Switch to Normal Mode to implement.

Clear context between unrelated tasks

/clear between tasks. Long sessions with irrelevant context reduce performance.

After two failed corrections, start fresh

Run /clear and write a better initial prompt incorporating what you learned.

Use subagents for investigation

Delegate research so exploration doesn't consume your main context.

Keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines

Ruthlessly prune. If Claude already does it without the rule, delete it.

Name your sessions

/rename auth-refactor — find them later with claude --resume auth-refactor.
